evidence: Ter. Haut. 587: Vah! quasi dēsit locus.
Plaut. Amph. 579b–580: Vah, apage tē ā mē.
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: astonishment, joy, anger; with apage or a scornful remark it is contempt.
Lewis & Short: “pish! tush!”; Syrus pooh-poohing Demea’s pride in his son.

terms.register: vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter. (Lewis & Short: never in Cicero)
evidence: Plaut. Amph. 310: Apage, nōn placet mē hoc noctis ēsse
terms.comment: See also go away and yucky.
The stock lament over the way things are going; said of small scandals it is the Latinist’s “tut-tut”.

phrases.latin: Abī deambulātum. — Deambulātum quō? — Vah! quasi dēsit locus.
phrases.english: Go for a walk. — A walk where? — Pah! as if there were nowhere to go.

phrases.latin: Syre, praeceptōrum plēnus istōrum ille. — Phy. — Domī habuit unde disceret.
phrases.english: He’s full of those precepts, Syrus. — Pooh! — He had someone at home to learn from.
